title: IN PHOTOS | Hudson Williams, Michelle Yeoh promote projects at TIFF
summary: See highlights from the Toronto International Film Festival, featuring nearly 300 titles, 800 guests and thousands of industry delegates during the 11-day event that started on Thursday.

image.caption: Hudson Williams and Carrie-Anne Moss promote their series, Yaga; Michelle Yeoh and Antonio Banderas attend film premieres at the Toronto International Film Festival on Thursday. (Carlos Osorio/Reuters, Evan Mitsui/CBC, Harold Feng/Getty Images, Shawn Goldberg/Getty Images)

blocks.text: Film fans and stars are flocking to Canada's largest city for the Toronto International Film Festival. The 51st edition of TIFF, which runs for 11 days until Sept. 20, features nearly 300 titles and big-name actors, including Javier Bardem, Cynthia Erivo and Seth Rogen, among others.
Each day, we will feature highlights from red carpet premieres, fan excitement and other festival moments, so keep scrolling.

items: TIFF's at a turning point — but how will the film festival's new focus on dealmaking affect fans?

blocks.text: Day 8: Sept. 17

Canadian actors Hudson Williams, Carrie-Anne Moss (second photo) and Noah Reid (far left in third photo) attend the red carpet premiere of their series, Yaga. This adaptation of Kat Sandler’s award-winning play unfurls the truth behind a mysterious disappearance in a small coastal town.
(Carlos Osorio/Reuters, Evan Mitsui/CBC)
(Evan Mitsui/CBC)
(Carlos Osorio/Reuters)
Oscar winner Michelle Yeoh promotes her film It's My Time, a comedy about a woman on the road to magic-cube mastery.
(Harold Feng/Getty Images)

Antonio Banderas greets fans at Roy Thomson Hall at the premiere of Up Against It, which was directed by Trudie Styler (pictured in the second photo on the left, with her husband, musician Sting). The comedy stars Banderas and Eva Birthistle as co-parenting divorcees faced with an indecent proposal.
(Shawn Goldberg/Getty Images)
(Chris Young/The Canadian Press)
Shuhua Yeh waves to fans at the premiere of Happily Ever After at the Royal Alexandra Theatre.
(Sonia Recchia/Getty Images)
Day 7: Sept. 16

On the festival's schedule today was Neil Peart: No One's Disciple, a documentary about the late drummer of legendary Toronto rock band Rush. In attendance: Rush bandmates Alex Lifeson, left, and Geddy Lee.
The animation gif shows Devin Kessler attending the premiere of Crystal Lake at TIFF Lightbox and Carrie Coon with fans at The Liberation premiere at Royal Alexandra Theatre.
(Harold Feng/Getty Images, Robert Okine/Getty Images)
Also screening at TIFF was The Man I Love, starring Rami Malek, pictured at the Princess of Wales Theatre, who plays an actor and performance artist in 1980s New York dying of AIDS.
(Robert Okine/Getty Images)
Malek stands with co-star Tom Sturridge at the premiere.
(Brian de Rivera Simon/Getty Images)
Malek checks a photographer's camera.
Day 6: Sept. 15
Ladies and Gentlemen, Brian Mulroney director Matthew Rankin, centre, attends the world premiere of his film at the Royal Alexandra Theatre. The film chronicles the rise of the former prime minister.

Tom Hiddleston attends the Canadian premiere of Tenzing, a story about the Himalayan Sherpa mountaineer who helped lead the first successful summit of Mount Everest in 1953. The film also stars Willem Dafoe (second photo), Caitriona Balfe, Thinley Lhamo (third photo) and Genden Phuntsok.
(Matt Winkelmeyer/Getty Images)
(Joel C Ryan/Invision/The Associated Press)
(Arturo Holmes/2026 Getty Images)

Penélope Cruz, Javier Ambrossi (second photo, left) and Javier Calvo (second photo, right) promote the Spanish-language film, La Bola Negra, which follows the interconnected lives of three men as they experience love and loss.
(Keito Newman/The Canadian Press)
Aimee Lou Wood, left, and Johnny Flynn attend the red carpet premiere of their film, The Idiot(s) at the Princess of Wales Theatre.
(Arlyn McAdorey/Reuters)
Oscar winner Kenneth Branagh poses with fans at the premiere of his film Atonement, a story of trauma and forgiveness following a horrifying event during the Iraq War.

Ink, directed by Danny Boyle, gets its Canadian premiere at TIFF at the Princess of Wales Theatre. The film stars Guy Pearce (second photo), Jack O'Connell and Claire Foy, and is about Rupert Murdoch's meteoric rise with The Sun newspaper and its influence on tabloid culture.
(Cindy Ord/Getty Images)
(Robin Marchant/Getty Images)
Actor Anna Díaz smiles on the red carpet during the North American premiere for Hombre al agua at Scotiabank Theatre.
(Mark Blinch/Reuters)
Actor Diego Luna waves to fans during the red carpet for Hombre al agua.
Day 5: Sept. 14
TIFF is now at the half-way point. But the stars are still out in full force today.
Oscar-winning married couple and stars of the psychological thriller, Bunker, Javier Bardem and Penélope Cruz (second photo) attend the film's premiere at Roy Thomson Hall.
Director Hirokazu Kore-eda attends the premiere of his film Look Back, which explores the life-long friendship and shared creative journey of two young manga artists.
(Frazer Harrison/Getty Images)
Director Takashi Miike, centre, and stars Shotaro Mamiya, left, Shun Oguri, right, and Lily James (second photo) attend the premiere of Bad Lieutenant: Tokyo at the Royal Alexandra Theatre.
(Cindy Ord/Reuters)
From left to right, Zo In-sung, Sul Kyung-gu, Cho Yeo-jeong and Lee Chang-dong attend the premiere of their film, Possible Love.
Isabelle Huppert poses for photographers at the premiere of All About Corinne at Roy Thomson Hall.

Orlando Bloom, as well as sisters Kate (in second photo) and Rooney Mara, are among the celebrities in town to promote their film. In their case, it's the buzzy Bucking Fastard, the tale of sisters Jean and Joan Holbrooke, who speak in unison, dress alike and fall for the same man played by Bloom.
Taraji P. Henson attends the premiere of Darlene Love: I Know Where I've Been, at the Royal Alexandra Theatre.
(Arturo Holmes/Getty Images)
Alden Ehrenreich on the red carpet for the premiere of the thriller A Talent for Murder at Roy Thomson Hall.
(Jeremy Chan/Getty Images)
Oscar-winning actor Helen Mirren, who was honoured at TIFF's Tribute Awards on Sunday, reacts with fans during the premiere of A Talent for Murder.
Cast member Mariana di Girolamo is photographed on the red carpet for the black comedy action thriller Wild Horse Nine at the Princess of Wales Theatre.
Wild Horse Nine star John Malkovich attends the film's premiere.
Day 4: Sept. 13

Léa Seydoux (first photo) and Lily-Rose Depp (second photo) attend the premiere of their film, Alpha Gang, which is about aliens that come to Earth to conquer it, and find that the human world has a plague they weren’t ready for.
Cynthia Erivo poses with fans at the premiere of Prima Facie at Roy Thomson Hall. In the film, she plays a British defence lawyer, who primarily defends those accused of sex crimes.
Annie Murphy poses on the red carpet at the premiere of her rom-com, All That She Wants. Murphy stars as a millennial, who hooks up with a Gen Zer.
Margaret Qualley promotes her film Love Of Your Life at the Royal Alexandra Theatre.
Amanda Seyfried attends the premiere of the American prison drama thriller The Life and Deaths of Wilson Shedd.
From left: director Yeon Sang-ho, and stars Kim Hyun-joo and Bae Hyun-sung pose with fans on Toronto's King Street West at the premiere of Paradise Lost.
Julianne Moore greets fans during the premiere of The Debut at the Princess of Wales Theatre.
(Rodin Eckenroth/Getty Images)
Javier Bardem attends the red carpet for The Beloved, in which he stars as an acclaimed film director who casts his estranged daughter, played by Victoria Luengo, second photo, in a period piece.

Channing Tatum, left, and Gemma Chan promote their film, Josephine, at the Royal Alexandra Theatre. They play the parents of a young girl, played by Mason Reeves, second photo, who are helping their daughter cope after she witnesses a crime.
(Leon Bennett/Getty Images)
Day 3: Sept. 12
Zaria arrives on the red carpet at Roy Thomson Hall to promote the film Misty Green, which was written, directed and produced by Chris Rock, second photo, who also appears in the film.
Lauren Miller Rogen looks at her husband, Seth Rogen, as they promote Babies, a film she wrote and directed.
Seth Rogen and Anna Kendrick, seen below, star in the film about a couple deciding whether they want to be parents.
Sarah Paulson poses ahead of the premiere of her film Closing Night at the Princess of Wales Theatre.

Courtney Cox, centre, directs Evil Genius, which dramatizes a bizarre 2003 bank heist by a pizza delivery man dubbed the "pizza bomber." Patricia Arquette, left, and David Harbour star in the film, which premiered at Roy Thomson Hall.
Day 2: Sept. 11
Fans of K-pop superstar Lisa caught a glimpse of her at the premiere of her documentary Always Lalisa at Roy Thomson Hall.
The cast and crew of The Stunt Driver pose on the red carpet at the film's premiere. The film stars Jay Baruchel, in the centre, pointing, and Ed Helms, to his left.
Director Michael Dowse, to Baruchel's right, says he knew Baruchel was perfect for the role of Canadian daredevil Ken Carter after watching him in the film Blackberry.
Baruchel with his wife Rebecca-Jo Dunham-Baruchel.

Rebel Wilson, left, with her wife, Ramona Agruma-Wilson, promotes Girl Group, a film she wrote, directed and starred in alongside Jennifer Coolidge and Randall Park, in second photo, at Roy Thomson Hall.
Actor James McAvoy signs autographs ahead of the premiere of his supernatural drama Faith at the Royal Alexandra Theatre.
Faith co-star Smylie Bradwell, right, who plays the son of a single mom, attends the premiere.
Earlier Friday at Roy Thomson Hall, director Adrian Buitenhuis arrives to promote the film Man in Motion: The Rick Hansen Story.
Hansen arrives on the red carpet.
Day 1: Sept. 10
Workers roll out the red carpet ahead of Thursday's opening film Being Heumann by Oscar-winning director Siân Heder, as well as the Canadian premieres for Fjord, The Housewife and Stuffed.
Furry friends and visitors pose for photos in front of the TIFF sign on King Street West, a section of which is blocked off during the first part of the festival and known as Festival Street.
(Carlos Osorio/Reuters, Joel C Ryan/Invision/The Associated Press)

At Roy Thomson Hall, the cast and crew of Being Heumann pose on the red carpet ahead of its premiere. The biographical film is about the so-called mother of the disability rights movement, Judy Heumann.
Actor Rio Finnegan attends the film's premiere.
Actor Fan Bingbing, who is a TIFF 2026 Tribute Award honouree, attends the film's premiere.
Toronto Mayor Olivia Chow also attends the premiere.
At the Royal Alexandra Theatre, actor Jodie Comer of Killing Eve fame attends the premiere of Stuffed.
And the film's director and co-writer Theo Rhys meets fans at the premiere.
Later at the Royal Alexandra Theatre, actor Naomi Watts greets fans as she attends the red carpet for her film The Housewife, directed by Canaadian filmmaker Ben Shirinian.
The Housewife is a historical drama based on a true story that focuses on a couple played by Watts and Luke Evans, also at the premiere.
